# Econ Agent Skills (Jonas Weinert)

license: `CC0-1.0 per the repo LICENSE file and README ("CC0 1.0 — public domain"); GitHub's API reports the licence as NOASSERTION / "Other" — record both` · 11 skills · last update: 2026-05-05

**Source:** <https://github.com/JonasWeinert/EconAgentSkills>

**Maintainers:** Jonas Weinert (JonasWeinert on GitHub)

**Related project entry:** [`econ-agent-skills`](../projects/econ-agent-skills.md)

**Compatibility:** `claude-code` `cursor` `codex` `gemini-cli`

> Ten opinionated SKILL.md skills across four workflow stages — data (working-with-data, api-data-fetcher, stata-data-cleaning), analysis (r-econometrics, stata-regression, python-panel-data), writing (academic-paper-writer, latex-tables), and communication (econ-visualization, beamer-presentation) — plus the repo-wide AGENT_POLICY.md decision ladder, cataloged here as an eleventh entry because the README calls it "the most important file in the project" and every skill defers to it. The opinions are the whole point: each analysis skill carries a decision tree that pins the agent to the modern DiD literature (Callaway-Sant'Anna, Sun-Abraham, Borusyak-Jaravel-Spiess, de Chaisemartin-D'Haultfoeuille, with at least two estimators reported) instead of the 2010-era TWFE it would otherwise reach for, to weak-IV-robust Anderson-Rubin inference instead of "first-stage F > 10", to rdrobust at the MSE-optimal bandwidth for RDD, and to wild cluster bootstrap below roughly 30 clusters — while DIME Analytics conventions (iefolder, iecodebook, ieboilstart, master do-files, immutable raw data, the four-tier replicability standard, the Reviewing Graphs and Submit Table checklists) supply the reproducibility layer, translated to Python, R, and LaTeX where DIME's own guidance is Stata-only. Three caveats a user should know. First, licensing: the repo LICENSE is the full CC0 1.0 text and the README says "CC0 1.0 — public domain", but GitHub's licence API reports NOASSERTION, so the public-domain dedication is the maintainer's stated intent rather than a platform-detected licence. Second, `academic-paper-writer` and `beamer-presentation` cross-link to a `latex-econ-model` skill that does not exist anywhere in the repo — a dangling reference, not a missing install. Third, the framing as an econometrics pack undersells the spread: four of the ten skills are writing and presentation rather than estimation. Upstream each skill also ships a deeper `reference.md` and runnable `examples/` (R, Python, Stata, Julia, LaTeX); only the SKILL.md routing layer is bundled here. The repo has been unchanged since 2026-05-05.
